newsitem.title: GREECE: Forex inflows push rates down in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Forex inflows push rates down in late trade.

text.p: Forex inflows estimated between 200 and 250 million ecus at the fixing helped drive money and implied forex forwards lower and dealers said they expected the central bank to cut its overnight intervention rate soon.

"Implied drachma rates and depos are trading lower on forex inflows of 250 million ecus at the fixing," said a dealer at a private bank. "The market consensus is that the central bank will slash its intervention rate."
Ecu/drachma eased to 303.08/13 after the fixing but has firmed to 303.18/23 in late trade.
Greece said on Tuesday it was cutting its three-, six-and 12-month T-bill rates by 50 basis points to 10.50 percent, 10.80 percent and 11.50 percent respectively effective November 26.
"The central bank basically funds government securities at 13.40 percent right now. If it cuts its intervention rate it would mean cheaper funding for banks," said the trader.
The mark was quoted at 157.23/28 drachmas from Wednesday's 157.260 fix, the dollar at 239.77/87 drachmas from 239.920 and the Ecu at 303.04/14 from 303.160 drachmas.
